identity: a declaration's structural identity is its RESOLVED element set and nothing a generator chose: for a model, the wire name of every field it declares or inherits, each beside the SHAPE of its type (a list, a mapping, a union, a generic alias, or none of those), the VALUE it pins where the node pins one, and whether it is required -- asked only of a field that pins no value, because a pinned field is required here and defaulted to its own constant there, and the pinned value already says everything requiredness could.  For an enumeration it is the member VALUE LIST read as a set, which is the identity reading 10 already fixes for one.  A declaration with no elements -- a root model, a constrained scalar, an alias, a field-free class -- has NO structural identity and is reported as having none rather than given a key its contents cannot distinguish: a `root` field is carried by every root model in either tree, so a key that counted it would make 11 declarations of ours one subject
